title: Proportional alert throttler and runbook orchestrator
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: Over the last 6 months we've seen a steady increase in low-signal alerts during multiregion transient events. This noise causes on-call fatigue and slows response to true SLO degradations. We need a platform-level solution that reduces noisy pages while preserving fast escalation for high-impact SLO breaches and supporting automated, context-aware runbook execution.
proposal_summary: Implement a proportional alert throttler (PAT) that applies dynamic suppression weights to paged signals based on SLO impact, region health, and recent alerting volume, combined with a Runbook Orchestrator (RO) that can automatically execute safe mitigation playflows (circuit breaker activation, partial load-shedding, or routing swaps) in response to verified conditions. The PAT should operate upstream of paging and integrate with our alerting provider; RO should be pluggable to existing incident automation tooling and respect safety gates (canary window, dry-run, manual approval for high-risk actions).
design_notes: - Throttler algorithm: compute a throttle score = f(slo_impact, region_priority, recency_penalty, correlated_alert_count). Translate score into probabilistic paging suppression and notification bundling.
rolling_deploy_plan: 1) Feature-flag PAT in dev, run in dry-run collecting score distributions. 2) Enable RO in dry-run with automated actions logged but not executed. 3) Canary PAT + RO in a single low-traffic region for 48h, monitor missed-alerts metric. 4) Gradual region rollout with 2-stage enable (soft suppression then enforced) and opt-out per-service. 5) Full rollout with training & runbook updates.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: PAT could suppress a legitimate degradation. Mitigations: conservative default thresholds, 'safety amplification' where any signal tied to critical SLOs bypasses suppression, automatic rollback if missed-alert rate exceeds 0.1% over 1h, and a manual kill-switch in Console.
acceptance_criteria: PAT deployed behind feature flag and running in dry-run for at least 72 hours
RO executed non-destructive playflows (circuit breaker open/close, cache flush) in dry-run and logged outcomes
No missed critical SLO pages during canary (defined as no >5 minute undetected regression for P0 SLOs)
Pager volume reduced by >=40% for low-impact transients in canary region without increase in SLO error budget burn
Documentation and updated on-call runbooks published and linked to console
Rollout playbook validated by SRE rotation and Product Ops sign-off
implementation_notes: - Implement PAT as a small stateless service that subscribes to alert stream and emits modified page events. - Use Redis for short-lived counters (recency_penalty). - RO uses our existing automation bus and requires new action types for graceful load-shedding and circuit breaker orchestration. - Ensure idempotency for RO actions and audit logs for each decision.
